chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) narrated that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down an angel to the earth. So that angel walked until he came to a door where a man was seeking permission from the owner of the house. The angel said to him: 'What is your need to the owner of this house?' He said: 'A Muslim brother of mine, whom I visited for the sake of Allah, Blessed and High'.

The angel said to him: 'Did nothing bring you except that?' He said: 'Nothing brought me except that.' He said: 'I am a messenger of Allah to you, and He conveys greetings to you and says: Paradise is obligated for you'.
And the angel said: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever visits a Muslim, it is not him that he is visiting, but he is visiting Me, and his reward upon Me is Paradise'.

key_terms.زُرْتُهُ فِي اللَّهِ: visited him for the sake of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a Muslim brother for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: In this renowned hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a divine encounter where an angel conveys Allah's promise of Paradise to a believer who visited his brother solely for Allah's sake. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *Ziyarat* (visitation) not merely as a social act but as a spiritual connection to the Divine, emphasizing that the reward is directly guaranteed by Allah. It highlights the theological significance of brotherhood in faith as a means of attaining closeness to God.
